basic_info: 59-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up of chronic conditions (depression, asthma, diabetes).
present_illness: Patient is here for routine follow-up of chronic conditions, including depression, asthma, and diabetes. The patient reports persistent depression with ups and downs, self-tapering off Prozac due to side effects (sluggishness, stomach discomfort), increased asthma symptoms due to pollen and heat, increased inhaler use, and a recent slip in diet control for diabetes due to travel. The patient also mentions that he did not consult his psychiatrist before tapering off Prozac and is considering trying a different antidepressant. He experienced lightheadedness and dizziness, which he attributed to the heat. He has not made any changes to his diabetes management plan since the slip in diet control. He is still on his regular medication for diabetes but acknowledges that his blood sugars might have been higher lately due to weekend food choices. He is trying to get back on track with his diet and monitoring his blood sugars more closely at home. He reports feeling more fatigued than usual, with emotional ups and downs, but no significant changes in sleep patterns. He has not had any episodes of hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia since the dietary slip, but he has been monitoring his blood glucose levels more frequently at home to keep track of how he's doing. He has not had any recent exacerbations of his asthma symptoms that required additional medication or emergency care. He's been using his inhaler as needed, especially on hot days, but nothing too bad. He tries to manage it by staying inside when it's really hot and avoiding the pollen as much as he can. The fatigue has been making it harder to get through his day, especially with all the running up and down stairs or lifting things. He feels like he has less energy to keep up with everything, and his mood seems to dip more often, especially when he's tired. He hasn't really noticed a specific pattern, but it feels like the tiredness makes the depression feel worse. The fatigue is worst in the afternoons, and it feels like it gets worse when he's doing physical tasks, like lifting boxes or running up stairs. It doesn't really get better with rest, but he does feel a little better in the mornings after he rides his bike. I guess the physical activity helps a bit, but it's not enough to really fight the tiredness all day. My appetite hasn't really changed much, but I do feel less motivated to do things, especially when I'm tired. It's like the fatigue takes away some of my drive, and I just don't feel like pushing through as much as I used to.
